messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Bimodal posterior
parts:
Thought I'd share something I ran across. To my dismay, a model I was fitting proved to have a bimodal posterior. See the attached pairs plot. On the other hand, even though I had to set adapt_delta=0.95, I'm astonished that Stan was able to sample from this posterior at all.

BTW, this was a case where it was really important to pay attention to those "divergent transition" warnings. At the default value for adapt_delta you only get one of the modes.

If you're wondering, this was time-series data and a single-source-of-error state-space model with local level and local trend. The data have a clear seasonality with period 7, which is not included in the model.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bimodal posterior
parts:
Was this one chain?  If so, and one chain is exploring both
modes and you saw lots of divergences, then it’s likely that
there is a narrow band of reasonably high probability mass
connecting the two modes through which Stan is able to
explore.  It should show up more clearly if you draw more
samples.
